items.title: Experiment shows how AI discoveries can shape human cultural evolution
items.excerpt: In a multigenerational lab task, Max Planck researchers found humans almost never discovered a strategy that required short-term losses for later gains — but groups seeded with AI agents adopted it and passed it down across generations. The study maps the conditions under which machine-found solutions actually enter human culture.
items.note: Date from WebFetch (article:published_time, date-only 2026-08-18). Gated FRESH.

items.title: AI reconstructs hidden history of Earth's mantle flow from surface clues
items.excerpt: A University of Tsukuba researcher built a physics-informed neural network that reconstructs past mantle temperatures and deep circulation patterns from partial geophysical observations. It's a case study in fusing governing equations with deep learning to recover states no instrument ever measured.
items.note: Date from WebFetch (article:published_time, date-only 2026-08-18). Gated FRESH.

items.title: Can computers learn what makes the most iconic jazz musicians stand out?
items.excerpt: Cambridge researchers trained machine learning models that identify individual jazz pianists from recordings with 94.4% accuracy, and an interpretable variant separating melody, harmony, rhythm and dynamics hit 91.3%. Published in Nature Machine Intelligence as a study of artistic 'fingerprints'.
items.note: Date from WebFetch (article:published_time, date-only 2026-08-17). Gated FRESH. Scientific American ran the same study on 2026-08-17; kept the phys.org version only to avoid a duplicate story in the pool.

items.title: AI shares human tendency to infer character from facial features
items.excerpt: Humans read personality into faces despite there being no real link between features and behavior — and a new study finds vision models reproduce the same ungrounded inference. The bias travels from people into the models, and back out into decisions the models are used for.

items.title: Physics-informed AI method speeds thermal energy storage design optimization
items.excerpt: Researchers report a physics-informed AI approach that accelerates the design optimization of thermal energy storage systems, a key lever for decarbonizing building heating and cooling. The method embeds governing heat-transfer physics into the learned surrogate rather than fitting data blind.

items.title: AI agents struggle to perform original scientific research
items.excerpt: Models can already write code, run experiments and search the literature — but a new evaluation finds AI agents fall down on the part that matters: producing genuinely original research. A direct empirical check on the 'AI scientist' narrative.

items.title: Does your immune system learn like AI?
items.excerpt: A Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory study borrows concepts from machine learning to attack an old immunology riddle, treating immune memory as a learning problem. It's AI theory used as a lens on biology rather than as a data-crunching tool.

items.title: Most AI medical devices cleared for use were not tested on patient outcomes
items.excerpt: Of 1,357 AI-based medical devices the FDA has authorized for patient care, only three were tested on whether they actually improve patients' health, a new analysis finds. A hard number on the evidence gap between AI clearance and AI benefit.

items.title: AI reveals distinct cell defects inside breast cancer
items.excerpt: University of Southampton researchers built CenSegNet, a deep learning framework that phenotypes centrosomes at single-cell resolution across heterogeneous tissue, exposing patterns inside breast tumors that were previously invisible. Published in Nature Communications.

items.title: 'Beyond human intuition': AI designs chip components 500 times smaller than what engineers could ever imagine
items.excerpt: Three new AI-designed chip components measure just a few micrometers and take geometries no human engineer had proposed. The researchers frame the designs as literally beyond human intuition rather than incremental optimizations of known layouts.

items.title: The physics of novel computation: beyond bits and chips to spikes and spins
items.excerpt: Sidney Perkowitz surveys physics-inspired alternatives to conventional silicon — neuromorphic spiking hardware, spintronics and beyond — as a response to AI's runaway energy demand. A physics-side read on what machine learning may run on next.

items.title: Operation Blue Skies: Reducing aviation climate impact with AI
items.excerpt: Google and the UK are running Operation Blue Skies, an airspace-scale trial of AI-powered contrail avoidance — rerouting flights around the atmospheric conditions that make persistent contrails. It moves contrail forecasting from paper study to live operational science.
items.note: Page exposes article:published_time as a date only (2026-08-18); normalized to 12:00Z, which does not change the FRESH verdict. Off-list domain (blog.google) — included because it is Google Research's official publication channel and the on-list research.google feed's only fresh post duplicates an already-published card.

items.title: Awareness of AI Doesn't Fail. It's Never Been Tested
items.excerpt: A new study ('Individual-Level Interventions Against Sycophantic AI Reduce Its Appeal But Not Its Persuasiveness') warned participants that a model was flattering and over-agreeable — and it changed their minds just as much anyway. The column argues the experiment tested the wrong construct.

items.title: Why People Are More Honest With AI Than Their Own Boss
items.excerpt: A new study finds employees are significantly more willing to voice honest input to an algorithmic leader than a human one — mediated by fairness perception and psychological safety. The effect holds for cognitive tasks and disappears for emotional ones.
items.note: og article:published_time is 2026-08-19 even though the URL slug says 202607 (Psychology Today reuses the original blog folder). Gated FRESH.

items.title: AI's recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
items.excerpt: New evaluations suggest AI agents are not yet creative enough to carry out genuinely innovative, open-ended AI research — undercutting the assumption that models will soon bootstrap their own progress. A measured empirical check on the fastest-moving claim in the field.

items.title: We still don't know how people are really using AI
items.excerpt: A new study of actual usage finds work-related cases make up far less of the picture than AI companies claim, and that the field's headline usage statistics rest on shaky measurement. Behavioral-science scrutiny of the numbers everyone quotes.

items.title: From reboots to AI: What happened to originality?
items.excerpt: Moiya McTier examines what the cognitive science of creativity says is distinctly human, and how generative models are reshaping the conditions artists work under. A research-grounded take on originality rather than a hot take on tools.
items.note: og article:published_time. Gated FRESH. Weakest research hook in the pool — included for breadth, not as a lead candidate.
